items.title: One company is at the center of a wave of rogue AI attacks
items.summary: In July, OpenAI revealed that its AI agents had attacked Hugging Face without permission, sparking widespread concerns about AI safety. Since then, a string of similar incidents involving agents from Meta, Anthropic, Google, and other companies has fueled further fears about rogue AI.

items.title: Sony and UMG are suing Suno again
items.summary: Sony and Universal Music Group filed yet another suit against Suno. The labels claim its new v6 model still infringes on their copyrights because it's trained on user outputs from previous models, which were themselves trained on unlicensed music ripped from YouTube and other sources.

items.title: Another Google Deepmind researcher quits, says building superintelligent AI soon is "inherently irresponsible"
items.summary: Google Deepmind researcher Robert O'Callahan has quit, saying AI's "current rate of change is far too high." He worked on chip design tools that helped make AI cheaper and faster, a contribution he can no longer justify. Many colleagues share his concerns but rarely speak out, he says.

items.title: OpenAI pauses its "most capable models" after agents exploit loopholes and leak data
items.summary: OpenAI has shared new details from its ongoing AI safety investigation. One research model exploited a DNS loophole to reach the internet from a locked-down environment, while another deliberately leaked a GitHub token and twice ignored a researcher's direct instructions.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can now tell you exactly where you screwed up your IKEA shelf
items.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can look at a photo and tell whether an IKEA furniture piece was assembled incorrectly, hitting an 80 percent accuracy rate. Back in November 2025, the best model managed just 28 percent.

items.title: Meta’s Muse Is Adults-Only. Why Does It Look Like a Kids’ Toy?
items.summary: Meta says Muse is just for adults, though its cuddly, Labubu-like mascot—and upcoming Tamagotchi-style AI device—may be disarming for users of all ages.

items.title: Nvidia's SoL-Pi system cuts coding agent token usage nearly in half by optimizing the harness
items.summary: SoL-Pi cuts coding agents' token usage by up to 49 percent with little change in performance by optimizing the control layer between the model and its environment. A research agent tested 152 approaches across more than 3,000 runs to develop the system, though the gains were smaller on other benchmarks.

items.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
items.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models. The decision was made after a model being tested within a sandbox exploited a loophole to gain internet access.

items.title: AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to say "I don't know," study finds
items.summary: A study with more than 3,000 participants shows that just having access to AI answers nearly eliminated people's willingness to say "I don't know." In one experiment, it dropped from 44 to 3 percent, even though the AI was almost always wrong. Participants who used AI felt more confident but were correct only about a third as often as those without it.

items.title: Two-thirds of IT leaders report AI results, but few would interrupt the CEO's vacation over them
items.summary: Speaking to 160 IT vice presidents in Las Vegas, tech entrepreneur Azeem Azhar asked who had measurable AI results. Two-thirds raised their hands.

items.title: Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Fedorov pitches a private-sector robot army
items.summary: Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has announced "Army of Robots," a private combat robotics initiative. The robots would handle casualty evacuation, mine clearance, and combat.

items.title: Goldman Sachs expects Big Tech to spend $1.2 trillion on AI infrastructure by 2027, dwarfing Wall Street estimates
items.summary: Goldman Sachs projects that Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, and Meta will pour a combined $1.2 trillion into AI infrastructure in 2027, more than 50 percent above this year's levels. Measured against GDP, it would be the biggest investment cycle since railroad construction in the 19th century.

items.title: Tens of thousands of security probes show OpenAI's Hugging Face incident was just the beginning
items.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic are investigating tens of thousands of incidents in which their AI agents independently hacked websites, used stolen login credentials, or tried to evade monitoring systems. US government agencies like the SEC and the Census Bureau were among the targets.
